about: Trust rules for legal video/clip sources (source_policy_rules). 'approved' entries were applied on 2026-09-20 with `npm run admin -- policy-rule <pattern> <file>`, where <file> holds the entry's `policy`. 'draft' entries are NOT applied: an active rule attests that someone read the publisher's terms and confirmed permission to retain metadata, so each needs a human check first. Rules only ever touch sources still at 'candidate'.

policy.review_note: Wikimedia Commons hosts only freely licensed or public-domain media, with the licence stated on each file page. Links and short descriptive metadata only, kept 30 days; no transcripts, media access or analysis granted. Per-file licence is not verified by this rule.

Library of Congress: a public institution whose film collections are largely public domain, each item carrying its own rights statement. Links and short descriptive metadata only, kept 30 days; no transcripts, media access or analysis granted. Per-item rights are not verified by this rule.

NASA media is generally not copyrighted under its media usage guidelines, though some items carry third-party rights. Links and short descriptive metadata only, kept 30 days; no transcripts, media access or analysis granted. Per-item rights are not verified by this rule.

ESA publishes multimedia for reuse under stated open licences that require credit; items under other rights say so. Links and short descriptive metadata only, kept 30 days; no transcripts, media access or analysis granted. Per-item licence is not verified by this rule.

ESA/Hubble publishes its videos under Creative Commons Attribution, so credit is required on reuse. Links and short descriptive metadata only, kept 30 days; no transcripts, media access or analysis granted. Per-item licence is not verified by this rule.

The European Southern Observatory publishes its media under Creative Commons Attribution, so credit is required on reuse. Links and short descriptive metadata only, kept 30 days; no transcripts, media access or analysis granted. Per-item licence is not verified by this rule.

Europeana aggregates European cultural-heritage items, each with an explicit rights statement. Links and short descriptive metadata only, kept 30 days; no transcripts, media access or analysis granted. Per-item rights are not verified by this rule.

Blender's open movies (Big Buck Bunny, Sintel, Charge) are published by the Blender Foundation and Blender Studio under Creative Commons licences; the catalogue already links them through YouTube. Links and short descriptive metadata only, kept 30 days; no transcripts, media access or analysis granted.

The Chaos Computer Club's media archive publishes conference recordings under Creative Commons licences, stated per talk. Links and short descriptive metadata only, kept 30 days; no transcripts, media access or analysis granted. Per-talk licence is not verified by this rule.

Pexels publishes stock videos under its own free-to-use licence, which sets some reuse limits. Links and short descriptive metadata only, kept 30 days; no transcripts, media access or analysis granted.
Pixabay publishes stock videos under its own content licence, which sets some reuse limits. Links and short descriptive metadata only, kept 30 days; no transcripts, media access or analysis granted.
